Transport mode change

A greener shipping decision can create several trade-offs.

A company wants to reduce its carbon footprint and therefore replaces air freight with sea transport for many international shipments. This may improve environmental performance and reduce freight costs, but it can also change lead times, inventory, working capital, and service.

Benefits

Sea transport may lower transportation costs and reduce CO₂ emissions.

Operational effect

Shipments usually take longer, which makes replenishment slower and less flexible.

Knock-on effects

The company may need more inventory and more cash tied up in the supply chain.

    Key takeaway

    One logistics decision can improve one objective but weaken another.

    Switching from air freight to sea transport can reduce cost and emissions, but it may also create longer lead times and further inventory, financial, and service consequences.

    Cause-and-effect chain

    1. Transport decision

    Replace air freight with sea transport for many international shipments.

    2. Direct benefits

    Lower transportation costs and lower CO₂ emissions.

    3. Operational consequence

    Longer lead times and less responsiveness.

    4. Knock-on effects

    More safety stock, higher working capital, and possible service impact.

    ✓
    Remember:
    • Lower cost and CO₂ reduction are attractive benefits.
    • Longer lead times are the central trade-off.
    • That time effect can lead to more inventory, higher working capital, and service risk.
